label: 1-3 steps after an original-phase digit 2, early in the sequence
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase on the 1-3 steps after the digit 2 was input, mostly at t=2..5; it is essentially silent at t>=7. prev_tok==2 gives 15x lift and prev2_tok==2 gives 12x. The strongest activations come from several 2s at the start (e.g. 2 2 2 x ...), peaking right after the run of 2s ends (about t=3) and fading over the next 1-2 steps. Activation rises with the number of digits in the sequence. It does not fire in the copy phase, only weakly at the delimiter (2% of mass), not on the 2 itself at t=0, and does not depend on which token is currently input. False positives are mostly 2s that appear late, or steps 3 after a 2, where activation is near zero.

issues: The t<=6 cutoff is a little too loose. Precision of prev_tok==2 is 0.99-1.0 at t=1..4, 0.82 at t=5, 0.24 at t=6 and 0.02 at t=7. lag-2 and lag-3 follow the same pattern: lag-2 drops from 0.97 at t=4 to 0.20 at t=6, lag-3 drops from 0.78 at t=4 to 0.22 at t=6. Changing the cutoff to t<=5 raises test F1 from 0.821 to 0.851 (precision 0.879, recall 0.824, mass recall 0.951). This is a threshold tweak, not a missed class.

Lag 3 is weaker than the label's '1-3 steps' suggests. rel_tok(-3)==2 has precision 0.60-0.78 at t=3..5, compared with 0.97-1.0 for lags 1-2. Lag 4 has precision 0.15-0.27, so cutting off at 3 is right.

Missed activations (3.7% of mass on test) are scattered and low-magnitude, mostly ~0.0-0.05 of max at t=3-4. Firing with no 2 seen at t<=5 has precision 0.8%, rising only to 1.5% even with 2 or more digits seen. Firing with a 2 seen more than 3 steps back has precision 6.6%. Neither is a systematic class.

The rest of the claims check out. Copy phase has exactly 0 active steps. The delimiter holds 2.2% of mass. t=0 is never active, and t>=7 is essentially silent (242 steps). in_tok rates are flat (1.1-1.2x for every token). prev_tok==2 has a 15.2x lift and prev2_tok==2 a 12.4x lift. The top examples are all '2 2 2 x ...' and peak at t=3, right after the run, fading over the next 1-2 steps. Rate rises with n_digits. Adding the delimiter to the predicate (phase<=1) lowers F1 to 0.804.
